newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower on corporate failure woes.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower on corporate failure woes.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed lower on Friday as renewed investor jitters about corporate failures by smaller companies cancelled out early gains, brokers said.
They said Taeil Media 63830.KS was rumoured to be on the brink of defaulting on debts which had cast gloom over the wobbly market, which had begun rebounding from recent declines.
The computer parts producer said Taeil had been facing temporary liquidity problems but it strongly denied the company would default.
The composite stock index lost 5.4 points to 733.64, off the day high of 746.87.
"The market opened firm on improved sentiment. But it was hit by more rumours of corporate defaults," said Park Sang-jae at Coryo Securities.
Taeil Media official said: "We are temporarily facing cash flow problems as other Korean companies have experienced. But it's not true we will default on our debt obligations."
Taeil went limit down, losing 790 won to 9,110 with 518,010 shares changing hands.
The jitters also hit shares in Ssangyong Group, some of which had been rebounding from rumours the sixth largest conglomerate suffered from cash flow problems.
Ssangyong Motor gained 220 won to 4,590 after hitting daily upper limit of 4,710.

Brokers said the carmaker was in strong demand because of negotiations on a cash infusion by Daimler-Benz and Saudi Aramco's agreement with its partner Ssangyong Oil Refining to extend additional payment guarantees to Ssangyong Motor.
But Ssangyong Cement went limit down, losing 720 won to 8,310 and Ssangyong Insurance fell to its daily limit of 10,400.
Brokers said the market was also depressed by lawmakers' demand in a parliamentary session that the finance ministry seek to disband a bank committee to protect against defaults.
Jinro Group shares gained momentum as creditors had decided to supply 36.9 billion won to struggling Jinro Ltd and extend its principal payments until September 30, 1998.
Creditor banks were still in discussion over the future of the other five Jinro Group affiliates and investors believed they would be bailed out.
Both Jinro Ltd and Jinro Industries hit their upper limit, gaining 230 won and 330 won to 6,450 and 4,490 respectively.
Jinro General Foods rose 60 won to 3,720.
Park of Coryo said: "The market needs more time to confirm its bottom line. After falling to the 720 level, I can forecast where the market is heading for."
But Choi Bum at C.S. First Boston said the market would rebound on Saturday. "I believe the market will stabilise at the current level."
